anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

apparatus: Catena/Pr insertion <καὶ ὅταν τῆς εὐωδίας αὐτοῦ ὀσφρανθῶμεν>.

bible_refs.note: He who has ears, let him hear.
Eyes and ears of the heart.
Your name is ointment poured out.
Taste and see that the Lord is good (LXX 33:9 χρηστός).

choices.why: Psalm 33:9 LXX; the pun stays in the Greek.

pass_a_gloss: For when from his spittle he makes clay and anoints our eyes and makes us see clearly, and when he opens the ears of our heart so that having ears we may be able to hear, and when we smell his fragrance, recognizing his name to be ointment poured out, and if having tasted we see that the Lord is good, and through the touch we handle him
pass_b_english: For when from his spittle he makes clay and anoints [our eyes] and [makes us see clearly], [and when he opens the ears of our heart so that] having ears [we may] be able [to hear], and when we smell his fragrance [recognizing that] his [name is ointment] poured out, [and if] having tasted we [see that] the Lord is good, and through [touch] we handle him
